title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase (+3.4%)
drivers.evidence: No past promotions at this price; higher price than regular ($5.03) likely reduces demand; historical promotions show uplifts only at discounts.

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day lost to sales; past week with closure shows ~10% drop in comparable product sales; no prior week with closure at this time of year.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.3. Halloween (event week) has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, but past data shows high volatility (x1.39 in 2025, x0.87 in 2024). The price increase to $5.20 (+3.4%) is above regular price and likely dampens demand. The store closure on Monday reduces the selling window. No past promotion at this price level exists. The classical model’s x1.0 is unadjusted for the price hike and closure. We apply a downward adjustment for price and closure, with low confidence due to limited evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.3 | 5%-95%: 6.4 - 45.5 | 10%-90%: 10.5 - 45.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
